skill.name: scientific-writing
skill.description: Guides scientific manuscript planning, drafting, citation formatting, figure and table design, and reporting guideline compliance.
skill.summary: Draft and revise journal-ready scientific manuscripts using structured workflows and established reporting standards.
skill.author: davila7

The other 60 findings are false positives from citation URLs, Markdown formatting, and ordinary scientific writing guidance; no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

content.value_statement: Scientific manuscripts require precise structure, evidence, and reporting standards. This skill guides drafting, revision, citations, visuals, and journal preparation through a structured workflow.
actual_capabilities: Structures manuscripts using IMRAD and supports alternative formats for reviews, case reports, protocols, and methods papers.
Builds outlines, then converts them into connected paragraphs with transitions and integrated citations.
Formats references using APA, AMA, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE conventions.
Applies CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, STARD, TRIPOD, ARRIVE, CARE, SQUIRE, SPIRIT, and CHEERS guidance.
Improves clarity, concision, objectivity, terminology, and section-specific scientific style.
Guides figure, table, abstract, journal formatting, and submission preparation decisions.
limitations: It does not verify citations unless paired with a literature lookup workflow and access to original sources.
It cannot validate statistical methods, numerical results, or scientific conclusions without supporting data and expert review.
The referenced schematic generator and research lookup integrations are not included in this skill package.
Journal requirements change, so authors must confirm current instructions before submission.

use_cases.title: Draft a first manuscript
use_cases.description: Turn a study outline, methods, and results into an IMRAD manuscript with coherent paragraphs and properly placed citations.

use_cases.title: Revise for journal submission
use_cases.description: Align an existing manuscript with journal structure, word limits, reporting checklists, figures, tables, and reference style.

use_cases.title: Edit scientific communication
use_cases.description: Improve clarity, terminology, objectivity, and logical flow while preserving the original findings and level of certainty.

prompt_templates.title: Build an IMRAD outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an IMRAD outline for a paper about [topic]. Use these study details: [details]. Identify missing information without inventing results or citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a manuscript from verified study information.

prompt_templates.title: Draft one section
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this [section] outline into connected scientific prose: [outline]. Preserve all facts, mark unsupported claims, and use [citation style] placeholders.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expand a prepared outline into manuscript prose.

prompt_templates.title: Revise a manuscript
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise the following manuscript for clarity, concision, and field-specific terminology: [text]. Preserve meaning and explain major structural changes separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing draft without changing its findings.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a journal submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt this manuscript for [journal] and [study type]: [text]. Apply [reporting guideline], flag missing checklist items, and audit citation and display consistency.

output_examples.input: Turn these points into prose: intervention improved response; confidence interval was narrow; no serious adverse events occurred.
output_examples.output: The intervention improved response rates, with a narrow confidence interval indicating precise estimation. No serious adverse events were observed during follow-up.

output_examples.input: Format this article reference in Vancouver style using the supplied author, title, journal, year, volume, and pages.
output_examples.output: Smith J, Lee R. Treatment response in adults. Clinical Research. 2025;18:44-51.

output_examples.input: Review this randomized trial Methods section for CONSORT completeness.
output_examples.output: The section describes randomization and eligibility criteria. It should also report allocation concealment, sequence generation, blinding, and the prespecified sample size calculation.

best_practices: Provide the target journal, study type, audience, word limits, and reporting guideline before drafting.
Supply verified source details and require placeholders when evidence or citation metadata is missing.
Review every generated claim, statistic, reference, figure, and table against the original study materials.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent citations, results, methods, ethical approvals, or participant details.
Do not treat polished prose as validation of scientific accuracy or statistical correctness.
Do not submit generated text without author review, source verification, and journal-specific compliance checks.

faq.question: Can this skill draft a complete paper?
faq.answer: It can plan and draft each section. Authors must verify every claim, result, citation, and interpretation before submission.

faq.question: Which citation styles are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers APA, AMA, Vancouver, Chicago, and IEEE citation conventions.

faq.question: Does it verify references automatically?
faq.answer: No. Reference verification requires original sources or a separate literature lookup workflow.

faq.question: Which reporting guidelines are included?
faq.answer: It covers major guidelines including CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, STARD, TRIPOD, ARRIVE, CARE, SQUIRE, SPIRIT, and CHEERS.

faq.question: Can it create figures and tables?
faq.answer: It guides selection, design, captions, and presentation. The referenced schematic generator is not included in this package.

faq.question: Should final manuscripts contain bullet points?
faq.answer: The skill uses bullets for planning. It recommends connected prose for final sections, except where a journal or method requires lists.
